utterances.text: Yes. I went to see General Adzic, and I asked that the JNA remain in Krajina. He said that the JNA would withdraw but that we shouldn't worry, because it would be deployed on the borders of Bosnia, towards Krajina; that he would professionally employ 10.000 men from Krajina in the JNA, in the territory of Bosnia; and if Croatia were to attack us, they would reach Knin sooner than the Croatian army could reach it. And I said, "General, do you think that Bosnia will remain in Yugoslavia when Bulgaria and Turkey have already declared that they would recognise the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina?" He looked at me with astonishment as to what I was saying, that that was nonsense, so that the army would remain in Bosnia. He felt that the army would certainly remain in Bosnia, although Bulgaria and Turkey had announced that it would recognise the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina and even though the Assembly of Bosnia had issued a declaration speaking about the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. If the audiovisual section could turn the -- turn down the volume of Serbian language in the English channel. It's very difficult for me to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be of assistance? That's what's happened to me in another day. You can regulate it yourself on your board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to this dispute about the Vance plan, did you have an exchange of letters? That is, Mr. Milosevic and you. Did you, in January 1992, exchange public letters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did exchange public letters, but we also exchanged private letters. On the 8th of January, a letter was sent by President Milosevic to me, and it arrived a couple of days later, by mail as well. And it was also published in the media, in the Politika and other daily newspapers, and on television. Several days later, I wrote my reply and made it public by fax for the office of President Milosevic, and a copy was made available to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put the Exhibits 79, 80, and 81 to the witness, referring to these letters. And as they're very particular letters, they have to be under seal and we have to discuss it in private session, as we are now. The Exhibit -- the Exhibit 79 is the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Which binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Exhibit 79, is this the letter that Mr. Milosevic wrote, and the exhibit tab 80, is it the letter that you -- your answering letter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 78, 79, seems to be the Politika article.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour. It's actually the complete -- in this Politika article, the letter is completely published. It's a complete publication of the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 80 seems to be the correspondence between the two, and 79, at least in mine, appears to be the Politika articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. 79 is an open letter to this witness from Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness actually has -- the problem is I have, for some reason, only the B/C/S version and it's Cyrillic and I can't read it, therefore I could only guess what it was. I'm sorry. This is -- Your Honour, you are correct. 79 is the original letter from Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the original letters actually with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. They are with my attorney, who is here present.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder whether we would need the original letters. If you would like to have a look at it or if we could deal with these copies as they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Unless there's any dispute about it, it seems to me for the moment we can go on with the copies which we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I think so too. Actually, I don't want to go into the details of these letters because they speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What I only would like to know from you, Witness: Did you understand these letters to be a threat, or include any threats for your dismissal from your position you had at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is stated in the letter of Slobodan Milosevic that I should be replaced, and others elected, or rather, it is stated in a particular manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And what was your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last sentence, it is stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the last -- where do you find this remark? Can you please read it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last sentence in the letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Please read the sentence that you understand to be a request for your dismissal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in the letter: "The assistance of Serbia to the people of Krajina will not be called in question in peace even, but the citizens of Krajina need to know that, by their actions, they have lost all our confidence and that in the future, for relations with the authorities in the republics of Serbia, they must delegate people for whom the national interests will be above personal political prestige."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was your response to this in your own letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my letter, I said that I considered that to be a call for my replacement or dismissal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do not need to go into more details because the letters actually speak for themselves. Witness, did you also then take part in the extended Presidency session on the 31st of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for three days, and on the 1st and 2nd of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have already heard from another witness details on this meeting, but I still would like to speak about a few points with you as well. You said it lasted for three days. Were you able to leave the meeting as you wished, or were you not allowed to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Everyone could leave it except me. I had to stay at the meeting until I stated that I favoured the complete and unconditional acceptance of the Vance plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who said that to you, or in which way were you forced to stay on until you changed your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Kostic and Borisav Jovic were chairing the meeting that was attended by the members of the Presidency, the General Staff, and other participants. The meeting was conducted in such a way that the session continued, and it was telecast directly with two cameras, and the public was aware of the session going on. During the meeting, somebody said to me that Milosevic had ordered that I shouldn't leave the meeting, that I may not leave the meeting until I agree to the Vance plan. And it was conducted in such a way that it went on and on. There were just two breaks for members of the government to come, the presidents of municipalities. The second break -- in the second break, I was allowed to go and call in presidents of the municipalities, and actually, I didn't come back. That is when I walked out. In fact, I fled from the meeting on the third day.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that someone told you that Mr. Milosevic had said you are not supposed to leave. Who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was either Radoman Bozovic, the Prime Minister of Serbia, or somebody said that Radoman Bozovic had said that. Anyway, the information came through Radoman Bozovic. Jovica Stanisic told me later on, when we met in 1993, that Milosevic had given him orders to arrest me if I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was the occasion that Mr. Stanisic told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, at a celebration of the day of the police, in a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the meeting, or during the breaks of the meeting, were you intimidated, pressured, or threatened in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Borislav Jovic said that they could replace me and that they could do all kinds of things to me. And I said, "You can, but I have my position and I'm going to abide by it." General Adzic even wanted physically to attack a member of the government, calling him nasty names. This also applied to other people from Krajina, giving them names. And I was told this by participants, because I was outside the meeting hall, making an announcement for the public. Adzic was very angry. He couldn't wait for me. He asked that the meeting continue without me. However, Jovic and Kostic didn't want to do that. He was so irritated that he wanted to physically attack people from Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you oppose the Vance plan throughout or did you change your mind at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I abided by my position up to the end, but in February I amended my suggestion and asked that we introduce complete protectorate of the United Nations, that is, that Krajina should be given provisional protection by the United Nations until its status was settled. I'm sorry; at the beginning of March, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Vance plan meeting that you discussed, you said you left it, you finally fled it. When you were gone, did someone from the Krajina government agree to the Vance plan instead of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mile Paspalj, president of the Assembly of Krajina, agreed, and he made a statement to the effect that in the absence of the president of the Republic, he had the authority to take over the function of president of the Republic, and in that capacity he said yes, the plan had been accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session again, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While Mr. Paspalj authorised -- accepted the Vance plan in the Krajina, the politicians in the Krajina who opposed it, did they continue to oppose it and even call for a referendum on the matter within the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Part of the Assembly and the politicians who were opposed called a referendum for the people to state their views about the plan. And the two questions of the referendum were: Were they in favour of the plan completely and unconditionally as the plan had been accepted by Kadijevic, Milosevic and Jovic -- no, I beg your pardon, Tudjman was the third one -- or whether they were in favour of a modified plan, following the lines of the Krajina government draft.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you have already mentioned the Assembly session in Glina on the 9th. And this Assembly session, was it an official Assembly session called by the president of the Assembly? Did all Assembly members take part in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them did. My information told me that it was a minority, in fact, which participated. But the delegation from Belgrade did take part.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned the delegation from Belgrade did take part. Who took part from Belgrade in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the Presidency of the SFRY, Branko Kostic and Yugoslav Kostic; the head of the General Staff, Adzic; and several other generals and their escorts and the people who accompanied them; the ministers and people from Serbia. Actually, it was a very numerous delegation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have prepared tab 88 of the Exhibit 352, and it is a video. A part, a small speech given on this Glina session by the president of the Presidency, Kostic, or rather, vice-president, and the translation of what is said you actually have under this tab. It will only be -- you have actually the speech, the entire speech, but we will only play the section page 35, the last paragraph, to page 36, the middle of the page. And when you are ready in the technical booth, we could do that now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is this the Belgrade delegation arriving, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is; Branko Kostic, Adzic, and his escorts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise but they do not have the text of this tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Mr. Kostic, good day to you. Welcome to Glina. You have come here to attend the Krajina Assembly. What do you expect of the meeting? Well, we have come and there are quite a lot of us here, and after a rather extensive discussion held in the Yugoslav state Presidency to take part in the work of the Assembly of Srpska Krajina and on the one hand to reject all the accusations, refute all the accusations that have been unfoundedly spread among these people, that we are leaving those people in the lunch. Also to tell the Assemblymen of the Serbian Krajina Assembly, as well as to all the people, that that is a crude lie, flagrant lies, that we have been and are remaining by the side of these people. In addition, to help inasmuch as we can, for reason to prevail, and that these people, as well as the Assemblymen, realise that that which has been gained through war until now can be defended by peace in the best possible way from now on, with the assurances of the Security Council, a world organisation, and the engagement of the Blue Helmets. Thank you very much on behalf of the Novi Sad television. Thank you too. Mr. Kostic, what is your message to the people of Glina and Krajina? That we have stood by and are going to stand by these people. However, choosing between the peace option and the war option, the time has come to defend peace, what these people have gained by war, not by continuation of a long and precarious war that might be spread out to the hinterland and Bosnia and sweep over the entire Yugoslavia or even wider in the Balkans. That can obviously finally result in the loss of everything that these people have gained by war so far. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can stop here. We can stop here. Thank you. Your Honours, as you can see from the transcript, there is following a speaker of the RSK Assembly on the conference giving a small speech, listing all the people that are present there from Belgrade. That's actually following in that next chapter on page 36, and I don't think we need to play it on the video. You can read it and Mr. Milosevic can read it also, and the amici.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You already mentioned another Assembly session in Glina. Was there an Assembly session in Glina on the 16th of February, 1992, and was the then Prime Minister dismissed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The Prime Minister of Srpska Krajina was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The president of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the subsequent meeting on the 26th of February, 1992, was Goran Hadzic elected the next president of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did any officials from Belgrade attend this session? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that will Budimir Kosutic was there. I don't know about anybody else. They said that some people were there, but as I wasn't there myself, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness tab 74 of the binder Exhibit 351, and it is actually the decision of the RSK Assembly, dated the 26th of February, 1992, in which the SAO Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and the SAO Western Slavonia join the RSK officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do not need to go into details of this decision.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rather, note is taken that they have united into the territory of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Goran Hadzic, what was his position before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic, from the summer of 1990, was the president of the municipal board of the SDS in Vukovar. Later on, he was elected as president of the Serbian National Council of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. And then, subsequently, at the beginning of the autumn or at the end of summer of 1991, he was elected Prime Minister of the government of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was his profession before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that from him personally, but everybody said that he was a warehouse clerk, or rather, an official, a clerk, a worker, in some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. warehouse, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have opportunity to see him during meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite a few times.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he have the political skills and intellectual level to fulfil the position of the President of the RSK? You observed him. Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little difficult for me to speak about somebody's qualifications for a particular job, the job that he did anyway, but what I can say is that he wasn't particularly eloquent, and his political appearances did not correspond to the model we have, the image we have, of a politician. But people from Eastern Slavonia told me that he had been elected to these posts because he was brave and courageous in standing up to the Croatian police in Vukovar and that he first jumped up onto a tractor and thus became a well-known personality.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he actually the dominant political authority in the RSK, or someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the RSK, no. The authority, the power -- he had power and authority. Milan Martic and his structures had power and authority, parallel structures, in fact, and they were the powers that be in that part of Krajina. Goran Hadzic, for the most part, spent his time living in Novi Sad. I don't know how far he was influential in Eastern Slavonia. He would come to Knin from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you speak about the parallel structure around Milan Martic, is that the same parallel structure with Frenki that you mentioned before, during the year 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, except at that time it was the official, formal authorities in power in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know -- you have already mentioned the person Stojicic Badza. What was his relationship or position in the SAO Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of Territorial Defence in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did he have an influence on Mr. Hadzic? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Hadzic made frequent mention of him, Badza, and a certain man named Jajo, as the main people that he cooperated with.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was Mr. Hadzic's relationship with Mr. Milosevic? Can you -- did you make any observations to this effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Complete obeyance. Hadzic completely obeyed Milosevic. He was in -- he completely obeyed Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was Mr. Hadzic's relationship, if any, to Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very close. I know that Stanisic would accompany him sometimes to the Presidency of Serbia, and people even said that he stayed in Stanisic's apartment, that he slept there when he came to Belgrade and that he was under Stanisic's complete control. At one time he was even said to wear a camouflage uniform in Belgrade when he went to meetings with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness the exhibit -- tab number 84 of Exhibit 352. It's a photo. Can we put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And looking at it, can you say where these photos were made and can you point out to us Mr. Hadzic, if he is on these photos, of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken on the 31st of January, 1992. It is the expanded meeting of the Presidency of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And is Mr. Hadzic on any of these photos; and if so, can you point him out to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are members of his government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you move it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of his government here. You can't see him on the photograph. But he looked like this man here, although this is Rado Leskovac, I believe, but they looked similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, then. He's not on the photos. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he isn't; at least, I can't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Usher, we can put that away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us the provisions of the Vance plan, and I would like to know from you now whether this Vance plan was actually -- if it was actually executed within the Krajina or the RSK. Was it implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the territories demilitarised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the weapons and military equipment and materiel was not taken away from the area completely, and most of the equipment was hidden, and through the Krajina police force, which was in possession of those weapons still, the military units and formations remained armed in the area. And also, later on, from the beginning of 1993, in fact, the heavy weapons were taken from the warehouses which were held by the peace forces, and from the beginning of 1993 onwards, the armed formation existed under the name of the Serb army of the RSK, although it existed from May 1992 in actual fact, this Serbian army with part of the weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were multi-ethnic police forces, police units, established? That is, Croats and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was the return of Croats to their villages implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not allowed to return, by the authorities in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you say "the authorities in Krajina," whom do you mean? In which way were they prevented to return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police prevented them, Martic did, and the political position taken was that they shouldn't return. This position was taken up by the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was Mr. Milosevic in any way involved in these reactions to the Vance plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean, please, and repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned that the Krajina authorities did not implement the Vance plan, and I was asking you whether Mr. Milosevic did in any way get involved in this action or influence the authorities in Krajina not to do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Milosevic did perform militarisation, or rather, he held the position that demilitarisation shouldn't be put into effect. Then he supported militarisation, or rather, the creation of military formations and the creation of an army, another army in Krajina, the Serbian army of the RSK. He appointed commanders, financed them, gave logistics support, right up until 1995, August 1995, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned that the JNA left the RSK. When did they start leaving the RSK, and when was the withdrawal completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The withdrawal from Croatia across Krajina began in the month of October 1991. Garrisons, Zagreb, Zadar, Sibenik, Sinj, and other parts through the maritime coastal route, which I didn't see, but I heard about them, and the withdrawal from Krajina itself, or that portion of Krajina, was completed in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness now two exhibits: Tab 75 and tab 76 of Exhibit 351.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Tab 75 is a decision of the RSK Assembly dated the 18th May 1992, amending the RSK constitution and law on defence to establish a Serbian army of the RSK; and the other one is from 1993, a decision of the RSK Assembly, dated the 20th of April, 1993, amending the RSK constitution to change the structure of the Serbian army of the RSK and its command. Is this the army that you referred to just a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I only want to refer to the document from 1992, and there is the Article 1, where it says: "The Republic of Serbian Krajina shall have a Serbian army in peacetime. The Serbian army shall comprise TO units in the event of the imminent threat of war, and during wartime, special purpose police units shall join the Serbian army." Which special police forces are referred to in this article? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the special police forces that existed since -- were in existence since 1991, and we've already discussed that issue here, talked about them. The ones that began to be established in April 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, this Serbian army of the Krajina, did they take over the property of the JNA and the weapons that were left behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Part of the weapons were hidden when the JNA withdrew, and in 1993 it was taken from the warehouses which were guarded by the UN peace keepers.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it an independent army? We have already spoken about financial dependence. Was it an independent army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was part of the military structures of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was the basis of -- in which way were they dependent, a dependent part of the structure of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of the commanding cadre, commanding staff, were active officers of the JNA who were on the JNA payroll. They were paid by the General Staff of the Yugoslav army and appointed to those positions by the personnel department of the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army. The commanders of the army were appointed by the president of Serbia and later the president of Yugoslavia - president of Serbia up until 1995, Slobodan Milosevic - and it was financed, logistics support was given from Yugoslavia. As far as personnel were concerned, Krajina supplied the men for the army and the regulations and provisions for it to be able to function.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to move now a little bit further in relation to meetings with Mr. Milosevic, and I would like to know if, in 1994, RSK officials took part in negotiations with the Croatian authorities. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When they went to meetings with the Croatian authorities, did they have contacts with Mr. Milosevic beforehand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes. His approval was sought, and the contents of the conversations, the discussions themselves, were determined by him. He would also follow the discussions as they proceeded and was informed of the process.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have to ask approval before committing to any agreements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes. It was a form of consultation. But actually, he determined whether something would be accepted or not, and what would be accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What would happen if anyone would not -- would take an isolated action without consulting Mr. Milosevic first? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't have been done, because those people would have been sanctioned and borne the consequences. There were even instances of physical jeopardy. People were put in prison who had independently made agreements with Croatia. The Daruvar agreement is a case in point, where people from Western Slavonia drew up an agrement with Croatia, and the (redacted) example as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the officials from the Krajina ever make an agreement with the Croats without an approval, beforehand consultation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Daruvar one could have been a case in point, but I'm not quite sure. What I do know is that the plan Z-4 was accepted through Ambassador Albright. Not directly, without Milosevic's approval beforehand, or prior to asking approval from Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which negotiations took place in 1994? What kind of negotiations were held with the Croats? Were they related to a political solution or were they just on economical issues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From mid-1994 until the beginning of 1995, there were -- they were agreements about economic relations with Croatia: The oil pipeline, supply of electricity, the water supply, the opening of the highway, the railway transport system.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did Mr. Milosevic allow you to agree to such economical relations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And he took a very active part in the drafting of the agreement itself, even with regard to the name of a mixed oil company that had been established.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to go now to a meeting on the 5th of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I have to ask for private session for this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you participate in a meeting in September 1994, together with Milan Martic and Mr. Mikelic; and if so, what was discussed on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that meeting. Jovica Stanisic, I think, was there. We were in Milosevic's offices, and he offered a luncheon in the same building, in a room adjoining his offices. In a strange, dark room. At the meeting, he criticised Martic because Martic had declared his support for Radovan Karadzic regarding the plans for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me clarify a matter. Who criticised Mr. Martic; Mr. Stanisic or Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic. He said to Martic, "I don't want to make a second Karadzic out of you." And he smiled. He smiled timidly. And he says -- he said, "Well, Babic is in cohorts [as interpreted] with the clergy," meaning in the political sense. And to that I retorted, "That is the spiritual dimension. That is my personal choice." I've just been reminded of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Mr. Milosevic criticised Martic because he had declared his support to Radovan -- for Radovan Karadzic. Report in relation to what -- support in relation to what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milosevic was exerting pressure on Karadzic and the Assembly of Republika Srpska to accept the international plan for a peaceful settlement for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in August, since Karadzic and the Assembly of Republika Srpska rejected the plan, he imposed a blockade, formally, on Republika Srpska. Milosevic did this.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in which way had Martic supported Mr. Karadzic? What had he said or done publicly? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He publicly supported Karadzic in rejecting the plan. He even went to vote, because there was a referendum after that. He went to Drvar, within the territory of Republika Srpska, though he was not a voter from the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said that formally Milosevic did not support -- or impose, sorry. Sorry. He imposed a blockade formally, you said. And did anything happen informally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that informally there was supply of oil derivatives and that the army of Republika Srpska was assisted by Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know on the basis of a meeting at Bijeljina that I've already referred to, when Stanisic and Karadzic asked me to make the payments.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, let me stop you. You do not need to repeat anything. Do you have anything in addition to that? Do you have any information in addition to that, that he continued to support?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, after arriving in Belgrade in 1995, that around Srebrenica, the army of Yugoslavia had been involved in the wartime events around Srebrenica. The army of Yugoslavia from the territory of Yugoslavia, across the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from Perucac, along the Drina, in Serbia, a place on the opposite bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned the Z-4 plan. What were the main points of the Z-4 plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main point, or the gist of the plan, was that the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, which had earlier been known as the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina and which was now known as Sector North and Sector South under the protection of the United Nations, should be given political, territorial autonomy within the Republic of Croatia. It would have a parliament, a government, institutions, a currency that would be special in appearance but it would be printed by the National Bank of Croatia, competence over the regional police and the courts, which would imply a high level of autonomy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who made this suggestion of the Z-4 plan? Was it an international proposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Z-4 was given that name because it was proposed by four ambassadors in Zagreb, that is, by the international community.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the transcript earlier on, it was said that -- it is actually on page 61 of the transcript, line 14, it says that Ambassador Albright accepted the Z-4 plan. Is that correct, Ambassador Albright?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ambassador Galbraith, the ambassador of the United States in Croatia, Peter Galbraith. He was the main creator and proponent of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This plan, did that actually mean the reintegration of the three regions of the RSK, that is, Krajina, Western Slavonia, Eastern Slavonia, into the Croatian Republic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Only the Western Slavonia would be settled immediately, whereas Eastern Slavonia, within a period of five years, and the territory of SAO Krajina would have a high degree of political and territorial autonomy in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the politicians of the Krajina in a position -- did they accept this Z-4 plan, you in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of March/end of February, the politicians in Krajina rejected the plan. The plan was accepted only by the last Prime Minister of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when you said March and February, which year? Is it also 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who opposed the Z-4 plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The President of the Republic of Serbia, according to what Milan Martic said, the President of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and he said half an hour prior to the beginning of the meeting with the international community that President Milosevic had said that the plan should not be even considered.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did Mr. Milan Martic consult with Mr. Milosevic, and of what time period are you speaking when you say -- when you refer to a meeting with the international community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was that week. I think it was the end of February/beginning of March. So the beginning of the week, Martic went to Belgrade for consultations. Whether it was Monday or Tuesday. And then on Thursday, an announcement was issued of the supreme defence council of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, in negative terms, about the plan, and then I think it was the following Monday when there was the meeting with representatives of the international community at which Martic said half an hour prior to the meeting that Milosevic had said that the plan should not even be taken into consideration. And at the meeting with representatives of the international community, Ambassador Farista Djijan [phoen] handed it to him. He wouldn't even take it into his hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On that occasion, then, did the Krajina authorities reject the plan, in that meeting then with the internationals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it was not even taken into consideration, so it was not accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We would need to go into private session for a meeting of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you speak with Mr. Milosevic yourself about the Z-4 plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, at the beginning of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the first to mention the fact that the plan Z-4 was a good one but that the territory of the municipality of Slunj should have been divided lengthwise. He didn't give any explanations for this. And then we actually discussed the events in Livanjsko Polje and the hinterland of Knin, the aggression of the HVO towards Knin. I've already spoken about that. And then he also said that there weren't 300.000 people of Krajina towards 4 million Croats but that there was the whole logistics of Serbia behind us, and that was that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you said that Mr. Milosevic was in favour of the Z-4 plan when you spoke to him; is that understood? He had only some remark in relation to Slunj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appeared that way, yes. However, one never knew with him for certain whether he really stood behind what he said; at least, I was not always sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have already mentioned this meeting in relation to the fighting that took place at the same time in Bosnia with participation of Milan Martic and his forces, and you mentioned the region of Livno and this gash and the line that Mr. Milosevic showed you to this effect. Was there also fighting at that time in the Bihac region, with participation of RSK forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I see the time. In fact, it's after a quarter past. Can we go back, when we come back, into open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And Your Honours, for your orientation, we are at the moment at paragraph 280 of the proofing summary, but I will also address paragraph 312, because it fits into the context and would speed up matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, Martic or RSK force participation in Bosnia, did Milan Martic and RSK forces participate in the fighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina already as early as summer 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, in the so-called corridor in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that the Posavina corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What is the importance of the Posavina corridor for Bosnia and for -- for the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina and for the Serbs in the Krajina region? What was the importance of this corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the corridor linking Bosnian Krajina and the Republic of Serbian Krajina with Serbia, or rather, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in which time period did RSK forces, with Milan Martic, participate in the fighting in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the summer of 1992. In June already they were there, at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who was in charge, in overall charge of the operations in the Posavina corridor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska and General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You have mentioned the fighting in 1994, 1995, in the region of Livno in Herzegovina, and my question was before the break: Did forces from the RSK also participate in the fighting around Bihac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who -- what were the forces on both sides? Who was fighting whom in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one side, there was the 5th Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was defending its territory, and it was being attacked by the forces of the army of Republika Srpska and the forces of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, consisting of the Serbian army, the police, and the state security service of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And - sorry - the forces of Fikret Abdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The forces of the police forces of the state security service of Serbia that participated, who led them? Who commanded them in this fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told it was Frenki, that he was in command, or rather, the DB from Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from Kordun, from the region, members of the government of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This participation of the RSK forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina, did this cause problems for the position of the RSK towards the international community and the Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1994 in particular, and in 1995, this compromised the position of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in relation to the international community, because the area of Bihac was a protected area by the international community.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did it increase the danger of an all-out attack on the RSK by the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the reason why the Croatian army and the HVO from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina launched an offensive to deblock Bihac. That was what was publicly announced by the authorities in Croatia in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it meant cutting off the Republic of Serbian Krajina from Republika Srpska and Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the RSK authorities and the Republika Srpska authorities actually have a military agreement on assisting each other in that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was an agreement between Martic and Karadzic, that is, between the authorities of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and that agreement referred to brigades of the army of Republika Srpska that would assist the army of the RSK. As for other parts of the agreement, I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit tab 96 of Exhibit 352.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document of the 30th of July, 1995, referring to a visit by Mr. Akashi, the special representative of the Secretary-General of the United Nations, and other persons, in relation to an agreement, a proposed agreement. The proposed agreement referred to, is that the Z-4 plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was -- this should have been a component part of the Z-4 plan, or rather, a precondition for the implementation of the Z-4 plan. So this was an agreement on the disengagement of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in the Bihac pocket; or, to be more precise, this was not an agreement, it's an announcement on agreement, announcement of approving the proposals made by Mr. Akashi to the leadership of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the proposal was that no troops or individual soldiers of the RSK would get engaged in the Bihac pocket, and refrain from any cross-border activities; is that what is proposed here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The person -- there is a handwritten note on it saying the 20th of September -- or sorry. No. Thank you. I withdraw my question. This proposal to disengage in the RSK, was that actually implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did happen? What was instead done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat continued. [Realtime transcript read in error "Maksic"] Mrksic nor Milan Novakovic, who was in command there, nor Martic nor the police nor the MUP of Serbia were they withdrawn from the fighting in that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the transcript, it says Maksic. Is that correct or -- in the document as such it says General Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Mile Mrksic, General Mile Mrksic, the commander of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can take this away. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, in 1994, did the Minister of Interior of the RSK have a problem to get control over the police in the territory of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did he --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of the Interior; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Who was the Minister of Interior in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of 1994, it was Ilija Prijic, who was replaced in that capacity, and the Assembly nominated, appointed, Mr. Perisic, but he didn't take up his post either in Eastern Slavonia or in the rest of the RSK either. So from the end of 1994 until August 1995, the RSK did not have a Minister for the Interior. One of the deputies was the acting minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did a delegation from the RSK then meet Mr. Milosevic to consult him in this problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. In 1995, April, around the 26th of April, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to apologise, but we need to go into private session for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you part of this delegation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who else was present? Who else was present from both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The delegation was led by -- yes, Borislav Mikelic, Uros Funduk, Slobodan Milosevic, Jovica Stanisic, as far as I remember. Whether there was anybody else, I can't quite remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you ask of Mr. Milosevic, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked that Milosevic allow Slobodan Perisic to be appointed, or rather, that Slobodan Perisic, who was elected the Minister of the Interior for RSK, should take over that function as Minister of the Interior of RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Milosevic's reaction to this? What happened at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Jovica Stanisic commented this request, and he said -- Jovica Stanisic, that is, "We have invested too much in all that," and he was thinking of MUP Krajina, "for us to relinquish it to somebody else now." And to that, Slobodan Milosevic reacted and said the following: He told the delegation of the RSK, that is, to us, "You must understand that we must assist you in this way, via the state security service, because it works in a specific clandestine way, and that's why we can't help you, assist you, through the public security service." In that way, he lent his support to Jovica Stanisic and his position on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was that situation solved on the day of this meeting? Was the -- could Mr. Milosevic help you in relation to the Minister of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The RSK was left without a Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put a document to the witness, and it is tab 97 of Exhibit 352.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document referring to Minister Peric and his position, and it is also referring to people and their affiliation to certain police forces. Who prepared this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we now in open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt about this document from Slobodan Peric. I got it from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, actually, at the -- the last paragraph, it says: "At all the meetings, Milosevic agrees that Peric should take over the MUP, while Stanisic immediately after that agrees with Martic that it should be prevented." Was the situation as described in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, I know what I have described. That was the situation. But yes, although I didn't hear that Milosevic had agreed, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there a problem in May 1995 in relation to the commander of the armed forces of the RSK after the Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have something to say, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't find this document, because in tab 97, the one I have, I have an announcement for Tanjug by the president of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, and not the document that you're talking about. So I have taken this out very carefully from tab 97.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Coming up. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no explanation for this situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's got a copy now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Good. Tab 97. I don't think I need to repeat this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just one more question in relation to tab 97. Did you provide this document when you had your conversations with the Prosecutor in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think you have not yet answered my question whether there was a problem arising in relation to the commander of the armed forces of the RSK after Operation Flash. Who was the commander of the armed forces of the RSK during the Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Celeketic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was he dismissed after the Croatian forces took Western Slavonia in their Operation Flash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes, around the 9th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you, in the Supreme Defence Council in the Krajina - I don't mean you personally, but the Supreme Defence Council of the RSK - agree about a new candidate, Mile Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to explain that the Prime Minister of the RSK, as member of the supreme council, Defence Council, proposed General Mile Novakovic for the new commander. However, Slobodan Milosevic refused, and he appointed General Mile Mrksic for the new commander of the Serb army of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did the Supreme Defence Council of the RSK agree? Did the authorities in the Krajina agree on Mr. Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It agreed with the decision that it be General Mile Mrksic, and this was formalised. It was officially stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to ask for private session, to clarify a matter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you see Mr. Milosevic in relation to the TO commander, the new TO commander, together with the delegation; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, about the 9th of May, or perhaps on the 9th of May, 1995, in the offices of President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When you went there with the delegation, who accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The delegation was led by the Prime Minister, Borislav Mikelic. I don't remember whether there was anybody else. Yes, there was [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mikelic make a proposal to Mr. Milosevic as to who should be the new commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He proposed General Mile Novakovic, who, on one occasion, was the commander, in 1993. He was the commander of the Serbian army of Krajina at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milosevic reject this proposal, or how did he -- did it -- how did it happen that suddenly it was Mr. Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He rejected it, yes, and he gave some sort of reason. And he also said it's been decided that it should be General Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know who made this decision that Mile Mrksic -- when you say he said it had been decided that it should be General Mile Mrksic, do you know who he meant who decided it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that Milosevic said that. He interrupted the meeting, left the room, and came back after a short period and said, "The new commander will be Mile Mrksic." Some people who were present heard mention of the Supreme Defence Council, but I don't remember that. I heard that Milosevic had said that Mile Mrksic was the new commander and that he had been appointed by Milosevic; at least, that's how I understood it at the meeting. When I said the Supreme Defence Council, the Supreme Defence Council of Yugoslavia was mentioned by some people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Open session again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the RSK government then approve the appointment -- or the decision by an official appointment of General Mile Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It followed the regular procedure via the Supreme Council of Defence for the RSK and the Assembly of the RSK as well, and that's how it was decided that Mrksic -- or rather, they adopted the proposal and verified it legally, that Mile Mrksic should be the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When did Mile Mrksic arrive in the RSK as commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was seen on the 16th of May, 1995. The Assembly appointed him between the 18th and 20th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What position did he have before he came to the RSK? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Guards Brigade of the JNA in Belgrade, and he was in command of it during the attack on Vukovar. And before that, he was something in the General Staff, held some post, but I don't know what exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When he arrived in the RSK, did he officially become an employee of the RSK forces, or did he remain to be employed as a VJ officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an officer of the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the previous two commanders that you mentioned, Mile Novakovic and Celeketic, were they also members of the VJ throughout their time in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During your conversation with the Prosecution in The Hague, did you review several orders signed by Milan Martic related to the appointment, promotions, and release of General Celeketic? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think we need to put it all to the witness. It's tabs 98, 99, 100, and 101 of Exhibit 352. They all deal with General Celeketic, his promotion and his release.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But I would like to put to you tab 102, and it's 102 of that same exhibit, 352. And that is actually a document by Dusan Zoric, the military post 1740 -- 90, Belgrade, from 21st December, 1994, regarding the promotion of Colonel Milan Celeketic to the rank of Major General. Can you tell us who this person Dusan Zoric is, what position did he have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was head of the personnel department of the General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia, or was the acting head.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have to go into private session, and I'm dealing now with paragraph 293 and the following two in the proofing summary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a conversation with Mr. Milosevic on the Z-4 plan in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a telephone conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At that time, had you discussed the Z-4 plan with Mr. Galbraith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with Ambassador Peter Galbraith, on several occasions, several times before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And immediately before you had this telephone conversation, what was the option given to you by Mr. Galbraith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He offered that we should accept and adopt the Z-4 plan and the disengagement of the armed forces of Krajina in the Bihac pocket. He said that we should accept a new mandate for the UN peacekeepers, which was known as the UNCRO mandate, United Nations Croatia, and that communications and roads be opened in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At that time, were you the president of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the Prime Minister of the government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Martic was the president, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did you not simply accept it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accepted in my capacity as Prime Minister, but I informed Ambassador Galbraith that this could not be put into practice without the will and acquiescence of President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How -- and did you then -- you said you had a telephone conversation with Mr. Milosevic on the 3rd of August, 1995. How did you reach him? Did anyone help you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jovica Stanisic did, from Jovica Stanisic's cabinet or offices.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you go to his office, and where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go to see Stanisic in his office, which was located in the building of the Federal Internal Affairs Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was present? Who else was present when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Stojicic, nicknamed Badza was there, and so was the head of the counter-intelligence service of State Security of Serbia, a man whose name I don't remember, but he resembled Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that the same man you mentioned earlier on to have seen in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. another meeting with Kertes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's the man, on the 4th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you explain to these three gentlemen that you wanted to accept the Z-4 plan and discuss it with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I said that I had accepted this with Galbraith, and they looked at each other in a slightly hostile fashion. They were a little hostile. But they did put me in touch with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Milosevic say to you in relation to the Z-4 plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He repeated -- or rather, he mumbled something. To give an example, it's as if he was speaking out of a dream. He just said, "Yes. Yes. Just slowly, slowly, everything should be conducted calmly." Those were his words over the phone. And he said, "Contact Vlatko Jovanovic. Consult him."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I met Minister -- Foreign Affairs Minister Vlatko Jovanovic. He was the SFRY minister in the ministry building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a technical correction. The witness says that I answered him calmly, and here it says, it's been translated as, "Yes. Yes. Just slowly..." So there's a difference between "slowly" and "calmly," especially when we're talking about war and peace. There's a big difference between the two words. So the witness said "mirno," and it was translated as "slowly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's to be noted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, what were the exact words that Mr. Milosevic said to you? Just to clarify this matter. What exactly did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Yes. Yes. Everything should be done calmly, or peacefully," "mirno."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did you actually at that time have time to do it slowly or calmly, or was there an urgency? What had Mr. Galbraith told you how much time would you have to make up your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, the witness didn't use the word "slowly" at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We heard. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, was there an urgency, a special urgency on the 3rd of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Reactions were to come the following day. I was to give a statement, and this was to be implemented, what I had accepted and what I was to make public by way of a statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you actually have an ultimatum from Mr. Galbraith to accept the plan right now, otherwise consequences would happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said what we could expect if we didn't accept, which meant a Croatian aggression, and that we could fare the same as Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you accept it publicly, and could prevent this aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I made a statement to that effect, that I accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was the RSK then attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, the next day, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit tab 103 of Exhibit 352, and it relates to minutes of the first session of the RSK government from July 1995, referring to the international negotiations. And there is no need to discuss it. It speaks for itself. And in addition to that, I would like to put to the witness tab 104 of that same exhibit, 352. It is a coded cable dated 3rd August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I would like to quote from this document. First of all the question: Have you been shown this document and been translated part of it during your conversation with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, orally it was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We need to know what this is, where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a code cable from the UK embassy in Zagreb, regarding a conversation between Ambassador Galbraith and the Prime Minister of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I'm afraid I have a record from the first session of the government under this tab.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Make sure the accused gets the right document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm just checking the transcript. 104.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I read this quote, we need to go into private session, because I just saw that it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The quote is: "RSK Prime Minister tells my American colleague that to avoid war he is ready to meet Tudjman's conditions and will announce this today. Unclear whether he has other RSK leadership on board. Milosevic being briefed by Americans on Galbraith's discussions with Babic, need to get Belgrade backing to lend credibility." Witness, was this the situation at that time, and is this quote correct as to your discussions with Mr. Galbraith?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of the fact that I don't know about any briefing of Milosevic by international factors. All I know is that a member of the French embassy in Belgrade had told me that Milosevic did not support us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if you look at the paragraph 9 of the same document, it says: "Galbraith assured us that he had the full support of state department." What is -- who are "us" here?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: "Us" is the UK embassy. It's actually a report of the US - sorry - the UK embassy, referring to a discussion of Mr. Galbraith with the witness and their further discussions on the matter and the considerations of Mr. Galbraith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was mistaken. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Milosevic after the attack, the so-called Operation Storm, on the 8th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, around the 8th of August, 1995, in the Boticeva Street, a villa in Boticeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The villa in Boticeva Street, what is it? What kind of a building is it? Is it an official building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the residence of the government of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you ask for this meeting with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initiative first came from Buba Morina, the commissioner for refugees of the Republic of Serbia in Banja Luka, saying that I should go to Belgrade to see where the refugees from Krajina would be accommodated. So I went to Belgrade. I reported to the Prime Minister, Mirko Marjanovic, who asked me for a statement. After I had given that statement, he linked me with President Milosevic and he made the appointment for meeting Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What kind of a statement asked he of you to make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Marjanovic asked me to make a statement to the effect that Yugoslavia was not to blame for the exodus of the Serbian people from Krajina. He even had a prepared text of a few sentences, and he also indicated what I should write down.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put the tab 105 of Exhibit 352 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is this the statement that you made on request of Mr. Marjanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
