utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do not need to comment on this further. Witness, and when you then saw Mr. Milosevic, what did he -- what did you ask of him, or what did you discuss with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to see him. This was on the eve of his departure for Moscow for a meeting with Yeltsin. First of all, the security would not let me in and then he came out and let me in, and we spoke in the room next to the entrance because in the conference hall there were other officials from Yugoslavia and the army. I could see this from the registration plates of the cars. This was a brief meeting that I had with him. I asked where the people would be accommodated, the people from Krajina who had fled.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What was his answer to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "In Kosovo." I asked, "How many people can fit into Kosovo? It's overpopulated, and there was ethnic tension." He said, "100.000, and many can also go to Republika Srpska and in Republika Srpska." And I asked him whether we could go to Eastern Slavonia. He said, "No, not for the time being." Then I asked him, "And where will the government go, the government of Krajina?" And he said, "Let it stay in Belgrade. If necessary, for negotiations. And you personally," he said, "you can apply to Mirko Marjanovic regarding your own personal needs."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the refugees from the RSK actually end up in Kosovo or in Bosnia and Herzegovina, or where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, that same day, as soon as the refugees started coming from Krajina, Ratko Mladic, the commander of the army of Republika Srpska, blocked the bridge across the Vrbas, and he wouldn't let refugees go any further. I went to see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We should go into private session for this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said you went to see Mr. Mladic. Where did you meet him, and why did you want to see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Banja Luka, because Mladic had blocked the way and prevented people from moving any further. And the refugees had formed two columns: One going from Bosanski Novi and Prijedor towards Banja Luka, and another one from Bosanski Petrovac, Mrkonjic Grad, via Manjaca, towards Banja Luka. So there was a block, and the situation was really difficult. Many had relatives in Vojvodina, in Belgrade, in other places, and they couldn't stay there on the road. And as far as I heard from the authorities of Republika Srpska, they intended to put up the refugees at the camp at Manjaca. And I went to see Mladic to appeal to him to deblock the road, and I went to see him in a building in Banja Luka. He said that he would lift the blockade but after Derventa. He said they should stay here in Republika Srpska. This is our land. And he did deblock the passage across the Vrbas, but then he blocked the way at the crossings into Serbia on the Drina and the Sava Rivers, where all adult males, able-bodied males were separated from their families and made to stay in Republika Srpska and the rest of their families crossed into the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, you said that able-bodied males were separated from their families. For what reason? What were they supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were integrated into the army of Republika Srpska, and those who had crossed into Serbia, they were arrested and taken to Eastern Slavonia, to a camp under Arkan or to the front line, the so-called front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean they were forcefully recruited into the VRS and into the army -- into Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where did those who reached Serbia, where did they settle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were accommodated in two ways: First, people who had relatives, close relatives, the first generation, could stay with their families. All the others were transported by the police to certain centres all over Serbia, including Kosovo, in columns of tractors or cars or in trains. I heard the stories of many people when they arrived by train in Pristina and other towns in Kosovo. They were flabbergasted and they took the first chance to flee from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, did refugees from the Krajina arrive in Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were Croatian inhabitants then driven out of Vojvodina? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some incursion into Croatian homes and throwing the inhabitants out; however, the Serbian police intervened and prevented people moving into Croatian homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to go now into an entirely different chapter, and that refers to Milan Martic. Was he arrested at some point in time in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there an arrest warrant against him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, issued by the Croatian government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness tab 111A.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, is this the arrest warrant, or rather, the decree, in relation to Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says here, but I know from the media that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you shown this document during your conversation with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, for your information, the Prosecution office received this document from the government of the Republic of Croatia in a submission in May 2002. With the help of the usher, I would like to put now to the witness tab 111B of that same exhibit, 352, and that's also a document that was received from the Croatian government, attached to the arrest warrant.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, it is a decree in relation to an investigation conducted into activities of Milan Martic and others. And did you have time to read this document? Did you read it during your conversation with the Prosecutor? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, there is referred to the Council of Peoples Resistance that you have already mentioned as being the source of provocations, and there is listed a lot of events from October 1990 through to April 1991, referring to attacks on the police, the Croatian police; the shooting on civilians, the destruction of shops, houses, and vehicles with explosive devices; and the attacks on railroad tracks. When you reviewed this document, did you find it to be correct? Those facts given in the document, were they correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Those people, or those properties that were destroyed, or people that were harmed, were they Croats or, as you mentioned also earlier, public property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were all Croats and public property, and Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That should be enough for this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When Mr. Martic was arrested in Bosnia, what was he doing there, and together with whom was he arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was passing through Otoka, a village inhabited by Muslims next to Bosanska Krupa. Also with him was his escort and people from the JNA, officers of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know what they were doing in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Where they were apprehended, was that a route used for the transfer of weapons and equipment for the military forces in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At that time, was that the only route that was open, or were there various routes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two routes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which routes were taken for the transport of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through Bosanski Novi and through -- via Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The weapons, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons came from two sources: One was Serbia, and the other was from JNA warehouses in the territory of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there also a military warehouse, or sort of, in Bihac, where you would receive weapons from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Zeljava.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that near the Bihac airport?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's actually the base of the Bihac airport.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: To receive -- to receive weapons from the Bihac airport, to whom would the authorities in the Krajina have to turn? Who would facilitate this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Colonel Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of security of the JNA Zagreb Corps, when I met him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just see that it's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, it is time. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, contrary to what was said earlier, we seem to have made good progress today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but there is one problem for tomorrow, actually, upcoming. It's not a problem, but it's a time-consuming exercise for tomorrow, because tomorrow we will go into the details of the Martic arrest and we will also go into a lot of intercepts. Today I skipped the intercepts to just make progress, but we have to come to the intercepts tomorrow, and I intend to do that in a group, because I think it's more expeditious to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We've been warned. We'll adjourn now. Could you be back, please, Witness MILAN BABIC, 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 22nd day of November 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
